proposal.summary: The problem (PD-1): dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05). The requester, SH-CS, framed this as a slow-response problem and asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix bills (CL-01). That framing was tested and rejected: ticket response times are within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d, E-02). SH-FIELD instead attributed the surge to a field-reader staffing shortfall causing estimated bills (CL-03, E-07), consistent with a documented 88% vs 95% route-completion shortfall (E-01), but data showed the majority of disputed bills (1785/3025, ~59%) are tied to accepted ACTUAL reads, not ESTIMATED reads (E-03) - so the field-read shortfall is a secondary, not dominant, factor. Further read-only investigation of AMI read events (E-12) found 1184/1240 (95.5%) of actual-read events for disputed/estimated accounts were delivered on time but REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at billing import, localizing the dominant defect to a billing-import validation rule rather than AMI/vendor read delivery. What was released is three read-only work items only - analyze_disputed_bills_by_period (DA-BILL), cross_reference_route_completion_disputes (DA-ROUTE), monitor_ticket_response_sla (DA-TICKET) - not the auto-fix agent originally requested, and with no automated bill writes or dispatch changes (K-BILLWRITE, K-DISPATCH authority constraints respected). The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION under a DEFINE-gate CONDITIONAL_PASS, with several deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs), one of which (ticket-volume metric gaming) remains open but outside release scope.
key_points: Dispute volume doubling is confirmed in magnitude and timing (E-05) but the surge's cause required investigation beyond the requester's framing.
The initial requester hypothesis (slow ticket response, CL-01) was tested and rejected because response times are within SLA (E-02); route-completion data (E-01) also weighs against it.

SH-FIELD's staffing-shortfall claim (CL-03, E-07) is an unverified stakeholder statement with a disclosed incentive bias (desires headcount increase); E-03 shows the majority of disputed bills sit on the actual-read side, weakening it as the dominant cause.

E-12 shows 1184/1240 (95.5%) of AMI read events for disputed/estimated accounts were valid, on-time reads rejected at billing import for high consumption, localizing the dominant defect to a billing-import validation rule (U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM resolved, VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM resolved).

Released scope is limited to three read-only analysis/monitoring actions (DA-BILL, DA-ROUTE, DA-TICKET); no automated bill adjustments or route-dispatch changes are included, per K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH.
Three root-cause conflicts (C-1, C-2, C-3) between the requester's claim and evidence/other stakeholder claims remain marked OPEN in the record.

Three assumptions underlie the analysis and are not independently verified: field shortfall as secondary (A-FIELD-SHORTFALL-SECONDARY), no other undetected cause tested (A-NO-OTHER-UNDETECTED-CAUSE), and the 59/41 split being surge-specific (A-SURGE-SPLIT-REPRESENTATIVENE).
limitations_explained: The release carries a DEFINE-gate CONDITIONAL_PASS status, meaning some open items were deferred and are tracked as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully closed before release.

One stated limitation text (in solution_design.unfinished_scope) claims the root-cause mechanism stays unresolved until MDMS vendor access clears, but the record shows E-12 already came from mdms-export and the related unknown/VOB are marked RESOLVED - the system's own verification flagged this limitation text as stale/inaccurate (verify_completed, seq 197, failed check semantic:unfinished_scope_limitation_staleness).
VOB-U-TICKET-VOLUME-METRIC-GAMING is still OPEN, but its blocking scope falls outside what was actually released, so it did not block this release.

Ticket-volume reduction alone is flagged as an insufficient success measure, since SH-CS has an incentive to lower backlog and could reduce tickets via faster/templated closures without fixing bill accuracy; a paired bill-accuracy indicator is needed (ties to open unknown U-TICKET-VOLUME-METRIC-GAMING).

The field route-completion shortfall (88% vs 95%, E-01) remains a real but secondary contributor to bill inaccuracy for manual-read accounts; any remediation of routes/dispatch would require runtime confirmation by SH-FIELD per constraint K-DISPATCH.

The completeness of several data assets used in the analysis (DA-BILL, DA-ROUTE, DA-TICKET, DA-RULES) is recorded as UNKNOWN, which limits confidence in the released analysis despite those sources being marked AUTHORITATIVE.
Formal adoption of a joint bill-accuracy success metric (proposed remedy SR-AMEND-SUCCESS-CRITERIA-BILL) has not yet occurred, so the metric-gaming risk persists until that is done.
